record.original_question: Fix c>0. Among isotropic composites made from an elastic phase and void, which microstructures in two and/or three dimensions maximize the quantity mu* - c kappa*, or at least form a sequence of microstructures whose values of mu* - c kappa* converge to the supremum?

evidence.quote: Problem 10: Identify, for given c > 0, in 2 and/or 3 dimensions, isotropic microstructures of an elastic phase with void that have the largest possible value of µ∗ − cκ∗ (or a sequence of isotropic microstructures with moduli such that µ∗ − cκ∗ converges to its largest possible value).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider linearly elastic two-phase composites in dimension d ∈ {2,3} consisting of an isotropic elastic phase (with prescribed bulk modulus κ > 0 and shear modulus μ > 0) and a void phase (zero stiffness), assembled in arbitrary periodic or, more generally, homogenizable microgeometries with prescribed volume fractions allowed to vary. By homogenization, any such microstructure produces an effective stiffness tensor; restrict attention to those microstructures whose effective behavior is isotropic, characterized by an effective bulk modulus κ* ≥ 0 and an effective shear modulus μ* ≥ 0.

Fix a constant c > 0 and define the functional F(κ*, μ*) = μ* − c κ*. 

(a) Determine the supremum of F over all isotropic elastic-void composites in dimension d (for d = 2 and for d = 3), as a function of c, κ, and μ.

(b) Identify explicit isotropic microstructures attaining this supremum, or, failing attainment, exhibit a sequence of isotropic microstructures whose values of μ* − c κ* converge to the supremum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying optimal isotropic elastic-void microstructures maximizing μ* − cκ* (a proxy for auxetic behavior with prescribed trade-off between shear and bulk effective moduli) is an active research topic. Numerical and computational studies of optimal auxetic isotropic microstructures with void exist (e.g., topology optimization, TPMS-based designs, homogenization-based recovery), but a rigorous mathematical characterization of optimal microstructures attaining the supremum of μ* − cκ* for arbitrary c > 0, in 2D and 3D, does not appear to be established in the literature. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Auxetic Properties of the Stiffest Elastic Bodies — Czarnecki 2024
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal isotropic microstructures recovered by homogenization tend to exhibit auxetic behavior, but no closed-form optimal family for μ*−cκ* with void phase is given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work considers optimal isotropic auxetic microstructures via homogenization but does not provide a complete mathematical solution to the μ*−cκ* maximization problem.

status_evidence.title: Obtaining auxetic and isotropic metamaterials — npj Comput. Mater. 2023
status_evidence.snippet: Automated optimization approach for auxetic isotropic metamaterials; results are computational, not analytic optimal bounds.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art is computational; the analytic optimum remains uncharacterized.
